description: The NBER-CES Manufacturing Industry Database is a joint effort of the National Bureau of Economic Research and the US Census Bureau's Center for Economic Studies, with annual industry-level data for detailed US manufacturing industries from 1958 to 2018 on output, employment, payroll and other input costs, investment, capital stocks, total factor productivity and industry price indexes, drawn from the Census Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Statistics and the Bureau of Economic Analysis. The NBER page (last updated 17 March 2021) offers version 2021a in 2012 NAICS, 1997 NAICS and 1987 SIC versions as Stata, SAS, Excel and CSV files, with summary statistics and technical notes; the data are free for any purpose with attribution, but not to be redistributed without permission. A Cornell codebook in DDI form (Zenodo, 2015, by Lars Vilhuber) also describes the variables. Coverage is the United States by detailed manufacturing industry. Caveats: the series ends in 2018, and industry definitions change between classification versions. For simulation it gives capital, labour, energy and material inputs by industry to parameterise production functions and input-output style models of how an infrastructure outage cuts manufacturing output. Related catalogue records include the EIA Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey and the industrial energy prices for 48 countries.
